userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for architecture focus area
userStories.notes: Seed story completed. Generated 11 architecture stories (US-82-002 through US-82-012) covering: error classification typed hierarchy, circuit breaker builder pattern, escalation metrics extraction, checkpoint keyword manager split, pipeline validator extraction, download orchestrator abstraction, pause calculator composition, checkpoint migration extraction, stage dependency injection, pipeline event bus extraction, and error pattern deduplication.

userStories.title: Introduce typed DownloadError exception hierarchy replacing string-based error classification
acceptanceCriteria: Create DownloadError base exception with subclasses: NetworkError, BotDetectionError, RateLimitError, FormatError, AuthenticationError in src/downloader/errors.py
Each exception class stores structured fields: category (str), severity (str), retryable (bool), original_message (str)
classify_error_category() in src/downloader/error_classification.py returns a DownloadError instance instead of a plain string category
is_network_failure() and is_escalation_error() use isinstance checks on the typed exception rather than re-matching regex patterns
All existing callers of classify_error_category() in download_segments.py and core.py handle the new return type without behavior change
Unit tests verify each error subclass is correctly instantiated from representative error strings
userStories.notes: Tier: foundational refactor. Implemented ClassifiedDownloadError hierarchy (extends existing DownloadError from types.py) with 6 subclasses: NetworkError, BotDetectionError, RateLimitError, FormatError, AuthenticationError, TimeoutError_. classify_error_category() returns typed instances with __eq__ supporting string comparison for backward compat. is_network_failure()/is_escalation_error() use isinstance fast-path when given typed errors. 24 new tests, all 188 pass. Files: src/downloader/errors.py (new), src/downloader/error_classification.py, src/stages/download_segments.py, src/downloader/__init__.py, tests/test_error_classification.py.

userStories.title: Extract CircuitBreakerBuilder for fluent dependency wiring replacing set_X() methods
acceptanceCriteria: Create CircuitBreakerBuilder class in src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py with fluent .with_escalation_manager(), .with_budget(), .with_caption_circuit_breaker() methods
Builder validates all required dependencies are set before .build() returns a CircuitBreaker instance
Remove set_escalation_manager(), set_budget(), and set_caption_circuit_breaker() methods from CircuitBreaker class
Update all call sites that construct and wire CircuitBreaker (in download_segments.py and core.py) to use the builder
Builder raises ValueError with descriptive message if .build() is called without required dependencies
userStories.notes: Tier: structural refactor. Created CircuitBreakerBuilder with fluent .with_config(), .with_escalation_manager(), .with_budget(), .with_caption_circuit_breaker() methods and .build() that validates config is set (raises ValueError if not). Removed 3 set_* methods from CircuitBreaker; constructor now accepts optional dependency params directly. Updated 5 test files to use direct attribute assignment. No production call sites needed changes (set_* were only used in tests). All 62 cascade+budget tests pass; pre-existing jitter/escalation test failures unchanged.

userStories.title: Extract EscalationMetrics from EscalationManager to separate metrics tracking from escalation decisions
acceptanceCriteria: Create EscalationMetrics class in src/downloader/escalation_metrics.py with methods: record_attempt(), record_success(), record_failure(), get_timeline(), get_summary()
EscalationManager delegates all metrics recording and retrieval to the new EscalationMetrics instance
EscalationManager constructor accepts EscalationMetrics via parameter (default creates new instance)
Timeline tracking (attempt timestamps, outcome history, tier transition log) lives entirely in EscalationMetrics
Unit tests verify EscalationMetrics independently records and reports metrics without needing full EscalationManager
userStories.notes: Tier: decomposition refactor. Files: src/downloader/escalation_manager.py (1,120 lines - god class, metrics methods scattered throughout ~lines 400-600 for timeline, ~lines 700-850 for outcome tracking), src/downloader/escalation_metrics.py (new file). The EscalationManager is a 1,120-line god class mixing escalation decisions, metrics collection, VPN coordination, and state persistence. Extracting metrics is the lowest-risk first step toward decomposition.

userStories.title: Split KeywordManager out of checkpoint.py into dedicated src/keywords/manager.py
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/keywords/manager.py containing KeywordManager class and SavedKeywords dataclass moved from src/checkpoint.py
src/checkpoint.py no longer contains any keyword-related classes or functions
All imports of KeywordManager and SavedKeywords across the codebase updated to new location
Backward-compatible re-export from src/checkpoint.py via __all__ or direct import (for any external/test references)
Unit tests for keyword save/load/list operations pass from the new module location
userStories.notes: Tier: separation of concerns. Files: src/checkpoint.py (1,340 lines - KeywordManager class ~lines 900-1100, SavedKeywords dataclass ~line 880), src/keywords/__init__.py (new), src/keywords/manager.py (new). The checkpoint module mixes checkpoint persistence with keyword preset management - two completely independent concerns. Splitting reduces checkpoint.py by ~200 lines and makes keyword management independently testable.

userStories.title: Extract PipelineValidator from PipelineOrchestrator for pre-run validation logic
acceptanceCriteria: Create PipelineValidator class in src/pipeline_validator.py with methods: validate_config(), validate_stages(), validate_checkpoint_compatibility(), validate_all()
PipelineValidator.validate_all() returns a list of StageValidationResult objects (reuse existing dataclass)
PipelineOrchestrator.run() delegates to PipelineValidator for all pre-run checks instead of inline validation
PipelineValidator is independently constructable with just config and stage list (no orchestrator dependency)
Unit tests verify validation catches: missing config fields, invalid stage order, incompatible checkpoint versions
userStories.notes: Tier: decomposition refactor. Files: src/pipeline.py (1,612 lines - validation logic scattered in run() method ~lines 200-350, StageValidationResult at ~line 45), src/pipeline_validator.py (new file). The PipelineOrchestrator.run() method is 273 lines mixing validation, execution, metrics, and progress reporting. Extracting validation makes the orchestrator's run() focused on execution flow.

userStories.title: Create DownloadOrchestrator abstraction to decouple download_segments stage from VideoDownloader internals
acceptanceCriteria: Create DownloadOrchestrator class in src/downloader/orchestrator.py with methods: download_segment(video_id, start, end) -> DownloadResult, get_stats() -> SegmentDownloadStats
DownloadOrchestrator encapsulates VideoDownloader instantiation, escalation arg application, and retry logic
DownloadVideoSegmentsStage receives DownloadOrchestrator via constructor parameter instead of creating VideoDownloader directly
The stage's _execute_download_loop() calls orchestrator.download_segment() instead of managing yt-dlp opts directly
Unit tests verify DownloadOrchestrator with a mock VideoDownloader handles success, retry, and escalation scenarios
userStories.notes: Tier: abstraction layer. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py (1,803 lines - VideoDownloader instantiation at ~line 368, _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts at ~line 962-989, download loop at ~lines 500-800), src/downloader/orchestrator.py (new file), src/downloader/core.py (VideoDownloader class). Currently the stage directly constructs and configures VideoDownloader, applies escalation args to yt-dlp opts, and manages retry loops - all implementation details that should be behind an abstraction.

userStories.title: Extract composable PauseCalculator from CircuitBreaker replacing 5-step pause pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Create PauseCalculator class in src/downloader/pause_calculator.py with composable steps: base_pause(), escalation_adjusted(), budget_adjusted(), apply_jitter(), cap_duration()
Each step is a standalone method that takes a PauseContext (dataclass with current_pause, escalation_tier, budget_remaining, config) and returns updated pause value
CircuitBreaker delegates pause computation to PauseCalculator instance instead of internal _base_pause()/_escalation_adjusted_pause()/etc chain
PauseCalculator steps can be unit tested individually without constructing a full CircuitBreaker
Existing pause behavior (values and jitter ranges) is preserved exactly - verified by existing circuit breaker tests
userStories.notes: Tier: structural refactor. Files: src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (633 lines - pause pipeline at ~lines 300-500: _base_pause(), _escalation_adjusted_pause(), _budget_adjusted_pause(), _apply_jitter(), _cap_pause_duration()), src/downloader/pause_calculator.py (new file). The 5-step pause calculation pipeline is tightly coupled to CircuitBreaker state. Extracting it makes pause logic independently testable and reusable.

userStories.title: Extract CheckpointMigrator from CheckpointManager for versioned checkpoint upgrades
acceptanceCriteria: Create CheckpointMigrator class in src/checkpoint_migrator.py with method: migrate(data: dict, from_version: str, to_version: str) -> dict
Migration logic for v0.9->v1.0 and v1.0->v2.0 moved from CheckpointManager into CheckpointMigrator as separate migration functions
CheckpointManager.load() delegates to CheckpointMigrator when checkpoint version differs from current version
CheckpointMigrator can be unit tested with raw dict fixtures without needing file I/O or CheckpointManager
Adding a future v2.0->v3.0 migration requires only adding one function to CheckpointMigrator (documented in docstring)
userStories.notes: Tier: separation of concerns. Files: src/checkpoint.py (1,340 lines - migration logic at ~lines 478-571, version checking in load() at ~lines 300-350), src/checkpoint_migrator.py (new file). Migration logic is currently embedded in CheckpointManager.load(), making it hard to test individual version upgrades. The Strategy pattern (one function per version transition) makes future migrations trivial to add.

userStories.title: Replace stage direct instantiation with constructor dependency injection for downloader components
acceptanceCriteria: DownloadVideoSegmentsStage constructor accepts optional circuit_breaker, escalation_manager, and rate_limit_budget parameters
When parameters are None, stage creates default instances (preserving current behavior for production)
Tests can inject mock/stub versions of circuit_breaker, escalation_manager, and rate_limit_budget
At least 3 existing tests are simplified by injecting pre-configured mocks instead of monkeypatching internal construction
Factory function create_download_stage() in src/stages/download_segments.py wires production defaults
userStories.notes: Tier: testability improvement. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py (1,803 lines - constructor at ~lines 80-120, internal instantiation of CircuitBreaker/EscalationManager/RateLimitBudget at ~lines 350-400), tests/test_download_segment*.py (test files that currently monkeypatch). Currently the stage creates all its dependencies internally, forcing tests to use monkeypatching for isolation. Constructor injection with defaults preserves backward compatibility while enabling clean test setup.

userStories.title: Extract PipelineEventBus from PipelineOrchestrator for decoupled stage lifecycle notifications
acceptanceCriteria: Create PipelineEventBus class in src/pipeline_events.py with methods: subscribe(event_type, handler), emit(event), get_handlers(event_type)
PipelineEvent dataclass (already exists) is used as the event payload with type field for routing
PipelineOrchestrator uses PipelineEventBus for all stage start/complete/error notifications instead of direct callback calls
Event handlers registered via subscribe() are called in order of registration
Unit tests verify event subscription, emission, ordering, and handler error isolation (one failing handler doesn't block others)
userStories.notes: Tier: decoupling refactor. Files: src/pipeline.py (1,612 lines - PipelineEvent at ~line 45, event emission scattered in run() at ~lines 200-470, hook calls in _emit_event() method), src/pipeline_events.py (new file). The orchestrator currently manages event emission inline during execution. A dedicated event bus enables external subscribers (logging, metrics, monitoring) without modifying the orchestrator.

userStories.title: Deduplicate error severity patterns between error_classification.py and common/error_patterns.py
acceptanceCriteria: Identify all duplicated error pattern definitions between src/downloader/error_classification.py and src/common/error_patterns.py
Create single source of truth for shared patterns in src/common/error_patterns.py
src/downloader/error_classification.py imports shared patterns from src/common/error_patterns.py instead of redefining them
classify_error_severity() in error_classification.py uses the shared patterns without behavioral change
Unit tests verify error severity classification produces identical results before and after deduplication
userStories.notes: Tier: code hygiene. Files: src/downloader/error_classification.py (275 lines - ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS at ~lines 117-131), src/common/error_patterns.py (shared patterns module). The ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS dict in error_classification.py duplicates patterns already defined in common/error_patterns.py. This creates a maintenance burden where pattern updates must be made in two places and can drift.
